t:
Section 12 of the Act of December 22, 1974, is amended by—

    (1) 
inserting, in paragraph (1) of subsection (g), the phrase “an independent legal counsel,” after the phrase “Executive Director,”;
 
    (2) 
amending subsection (h) to read as follows:


“(h) 
The Commission is authorized to provide for its own administrative, fiscal, and housekeeping services.”:



 
    (3) 
redesignating subsection (i) as subsection (j) and inserting new subsection (i) as follows:


“(i)

(1) 
The Commission is authorized to call upon any department or agency of the United States to assist the Commission in implementing its relocation plan and completing relocation within the time required by law, except that the control over and responsibility for completing relocation shall remain in the Commission. In any case in which the Commission calls upon any such department or agency for assistance under this section, such department or agency shall provide reasonable assistance so requested.


“(2) 
On failure of any agency to provide reasonable assistance as required under paragraph (1) of this subsection, the Commission shall report such failure to the Congress.”.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a "Commission" calling on others for assistance and reporting failures is participation. But the only actors involved are federal departments and agencies assisting the Commission, plus a report to Congress, all of which are inside the federal government. The rest covers the Commission's staffing (an independent legal counsel) and administrative services; no outside party is consulted on a federal decision, and no comment, hearing, rulemaking, or right to sue is provided.
fable.s: The Commission is authorized to call upon any department or agency of the United States to assist the Commission in implementing its relocation plan

opus.w: Everyone involved in this section is inside the federal government. The Commission can ask federal departments and agencies for help, and if one fails to help, the Commission reports that to Congress. Both are internal government steps. The 'independent legal counsel' is a staff position added to the Commission, not an outside party consulted before a decision. There is no comment period, public hearing, consultation with states or tribes, outside advisory body, or right to sue.
opus.s: The Commission is authorized to call upon any department or agency of the United States to assist the Commission in implementing its relocation plan
opus.b:
The tempting reading is that this is participation because it mentions "an independent legal counsel," asks other agencies for help, and requires a report to Congress. None of these brings in anyone outside the federal government:
- The legal counsel is staff hired by the Commission.
- The agencies the Commission can call on are federal ("any department or agency of the United States").
- Congress is part of the federal government.

qwen_chat.w: This section authorizes the Commission to request assistance from other federal departments or agencies. Since both the Commission and the departments/agencies are part of the federal government, this interaction is intra-governmental coordination. The definition explicitly excludes coordination between federal agencies from the scope of participation. There is no involvement of outside parties such as states, tribes, the public, or private entities in the decision-making process described here.
qwen_chat.s: The Commission is authorized to call upon any department or agency of the United States to assist the Commission in implementing its relocation plan and completing relocation within the time required by law, except that the control over and responsibility for completing relocation shall remain in the Commission. In any case in which the Commission calls upon any such department or agency for assistance under this section, such department or agency shall provide reasonable assistance so requested.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that the Commission calling upon federal agencies for assistance constitutes "coordination" or "consultation." However, the definition explicitly states that consultation or coordination *between* federal agencies or officials is intra-governmental and does not count as participation. The actors involved (the Commission and other federal departments/agencies) are all inside the federal government.
